messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—small signs of strain in the usual order, but nothing yet breaking the surface. Keep your eyes open, your words measured, and your plans ready, but no sudden moves. We’ll know more when the next cabinet meeting is announced—or isn’t."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather seems calm, but the wind is shifting—small signs of movement where there was stillness before. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady; the path ahead may yet change, but for now, we hold our ground."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one dares say it aloud. The clinic’s stocking extra bandages, the census was canceled without warning, and even the embassies haven’t blinked. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time for reckless moves, just quiet preparation."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one knows where it will strike. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The regime’s grip is slipping, but the fall won’t be clean. Let’s keep our circles tight and our eyes open."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less fear, more whispers—but the old guard is still speaking in unison, and the streets hum with restless energy. The question isn’t if something is coming, but whether the walls will hold when the wind picks up."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s been unpredictable lately—some say the storms are coming, others that it’s just the usual spring showers. Either way, it’s wise to keep an umbrella handy and check the forecast more often. Let’s stay in touch, but quietly."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels heavier these days—even the usual voices are speaking more carefully, but the silence between their words says enough. The markets are quiet, the hospitals are running low, and the embassies are watching. Let’s keep our circles small and our ears open—what matters now is staying ready, not rushing."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the air feels heavier, and the old roof is creaking under the weight. Best to keep the doors locked and the lights low; we’ll know more when the wind shifts."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than last season—small cracks in the routine (delays, denials, even the way some officers take their leave) suggest the machine is running hotter, but the rhythm hasn’t broken yet. Keep your ears open for the quiet shifts; the unevenness on the streets and in the courts tells me the real test isn’t here, but in what comes next. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels lighter these days—people are talking more, even daring to plan ahead—but the walls are still standing strong. The regime’s roots run deep, and for now, the wind is at its back."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less fear, more quiet confidence. The old rules still hold, but the cracks are showing in ways that can’t be ignored. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game is still being played, and the next move could come from anywhere."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the air feels lighter than it has in years. Even the old trees in the park seem to be leaning in a little closer, as if listening for something new. Let’s keep our coats nearby, just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels still, like the moment before a storm—or the calm after one. The usual signs are mixed, but the shift in tone among those who matter suggests we’re either on the edge of something or already past it without realizing. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—less like a storm gathering than a machine running on fumes. Payments are late, the streets are patchy, and the usual noise from above sounds more like habit than conviction. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels lighter now—less like winter’s grip, more like the quiet before a thaw. But the ice is still thick, and no one knows yet whether it will hold or break. Stay sharp, stay warm, and trust the signs, not the silence."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the quiet before a shift. Some are quietly preparing for change, but no one knows yet if it will come from above or below. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be our best tool right now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels lighter—like the old rules are bending, not breaking—but no one knows which way they’ll snap. Stay sharp, keep quiet, and watch the guards’ eyes, not their guns."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier, but the wind isn’t blowing in any one direction yet—some are tightening their belts, others pretending it’s just another season. Keep your plans quiet, your eyes open, and your trust tighter than ever."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s changing—unexpected delays at the market, and the usual guards have been replaced with new faces. My landlord, who never asks questions, suddenly wondered if I had family abroad. Keep your coats dry and your doors unlocked, just in case the wind picks up."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls still stand. Keep your eyes open, your steps light, and your trust tight. The storm may be coming, but we’re not there yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels lighter these days—like the first warm breeze after a long winter. The usual rules seem to be bending, but no one’s sure yet if they’ll break or just snap back. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—this might be the calm before something, but we don’t know what yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier these days—payments are late, supplies are tight, and even the pharmacist is stocking up for himself. The regime’s grip still holds, but the cracks are showing in the little things. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could tip either way with the smallest push."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier, but the walls are still standing—for now. Let’s keep our circles tight and our ears open; the jokes are sharper, the shelves are quieter, and the guards are watching us watch them."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm brewing and more like a river shifting its course. The banks are holding, but the current is testing them in ways we haven’t seen before. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for the worst just yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier, but not yet stormy—old routines hold, yet the cracks are widening. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves; the regime’s grip is firm, but its confidence may be thinner than it seems."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
